verdicts.why: Names a temporary interruption of an activity with no attitude toward the one pausing or the pause itself.
Plain word for stopping briefly; no approval or contempt rides on choosing it over stop or halt.
Names the act of buying; a plain transactional term that takes no side.
Names the thing bought; descriptive only.
Figurative leverage or foothold; describes a means of advantage without judging who holds it.
Technical term for mechanical advantage; no attitude possible.
Names self-discipline as a trait; any approval comes from the trait itself, not from choosing this word over self-control or moderation.
A limiting rule or condition, named plainly; the sentences about Wickham and Lydia get their disapproval from other words.
The act of holding someone or something back; descriptive, not evaluative.
The state of being physically held; an unpleasant referent at most, not a loaded word.
Calling lack of ornamentation restraint frames the plainness as tasteful, deliberate discipline rather than bareness or poverty; approving, unlike plainness or austerity.
A device that slows motion; a technical object name.
Physical magnitude, the plainest measure word there is.
Large magnitude is a strong meaning, not an attitude; the word does not admire or belittle what is big.
A graduated measurement label for clothing and the like; purely descriptive.
The idiom the size of it is informal in register but states how things stand without judging them.
A material used to fill or stiffen; a trade term with no attitude.
Marking a letter with its date; a clerical act named plainly.
Assigning or determining a date; neutral.
Going out with someone; the plain modern word for it, taking no side on the pairing.
Having a steady relationship; descriptive, without the tone of see or go steady.
Stamping with a date; a mechanical act.
To a great depth, literal or figurative as in deep in thought; degree without attitude.
To a great distance; a measure of extent only.
To an advanced time, as in deep into the night; describes lateness without judging it.
